tree: Sean Payton (huge influence) / Dennis Allen (hired him as Saints DBs coach 2016-20). Lions defensive coordinator under Dan Campbell.
Matt LaFleur: run game coordinator from 2021, with LaFleur praising his work coordinating the run game.
Dan Quinn. Quinn's Falcons (quality control, then outside linebackers coach) and Cowboys defensive line coach 2021-23.

known_for: Builds his defense around what his players do best and does not like to be painted into one scheme.

tree: Klint Kubiak. Succeeded him as Vikings QBs coach in 2021, followed him to Seattle in 2025 and the Raiders in 2026.
Mike Holmgren, who learned the West Coast offense from Bill Walsh. Reid learned it on Holmgren's Packers staff.
known_for: Blends the West Coast offense with spread ideas such as the RPO, pairing a timing-based passing game with a spread look.

tree: Vic Fangio: worked for Fangio and hails from his system.
known_for: Runs a multiple defense and talks more about play style than scheme. Jacksonville moved to an off-coverage scheme under him and used dime personnel at the second-highest rate in the NFL.
Runs a multiple, flexible defense built on the system he used with the Ravens.
Builds the offense on a detailed run game, with heavy play action, pre-snap deception and misdirection, and changes the plan for each opponent.

tree: Kyle Shanahan (on his 49ers staff 2017-2021)
Dave Canales: the only Seahawks assistant Canales took to Tampa Bay in 2023, then his offensive coordinator in Carolina.

known_for: Known for nickel-heavy defenses and a signature "umbrella" pass coverage. The Saints finished second in defensive EPA per rush.

tree: Mike McCarthy. Tight ends coach in Green Bay 2016-18.

known_for: Developed quarterback Josh Allen as Bills offensive coordinator, with a top-five offense in his last two years there. His offenses have often been strong running teams.

tree: Aaron Glenn. Lions defensive backs coach, safeties coach and defensive assistant while Glenn was defensive coordinator (2021-23).
Kyle Shanahan (49ers assistant since 2019; run game coordinator and tight ends coach in 2025)
known_for: Plans to keep Seattle's offense largely as it was, close to the one that won the Super Bowl, and wants it fast, violent and aggressive.

tree: Bill Belichick (over a decade with the Patriots)
known_for: Sends extra pass rushers at one of the highest rates in the league (about half of Vikings snaps), with a lot of zone coverage behind it and some coverage disguise.

tree: Pete Carroll: Seahawks offensive coordinator 2018-20, which he calls critical to his development.
known_for: Builds his offense on the run and play-action passing, which he says go hand in hand, and likes shifts and motions to distort the defense.

tree: Jesse Minter / Jim Harbaugh. Chargers safeties coach 2024; Western Michigan 2025.
known_for: Expected to run the same scheme as predecessor Jesse Minter; he ran a very similar version at Western Michigan in 2025.

tree: Raheem Morris / Brandon Staley / Wade Phillips (Rams defensive staffs)
known_for: Plans to keep the same three-four structure and core beliefs; calls the scheme a work in progress and says it is all about the players.

tree: Vic Fangio: worked under Fangio in Denver from 2021 and again in Philadelphia.
known_for: Runs a Fangio-style defense with his own twist, and is expected to use more two-high safety looks than Dallas did before.

tree: Bill Parcells (drafted by him) and Sean Payton (assistant in New Orleans 2016-2020).
Zac Taylor: Bengals assistant for eight seasons, promoted from quarterbacks coach to coordinate Taylor's offense.
Brian Flores (Vikings staff the last three years); also learned from Lou Anarumo and Vance Joseph
known_for: Brings Brian Flores's aggressive scheme to Washington, with more blitzes and a 3-4 base look, but says players come first: "4-3, 3-4, it's just numbers."

tree: Pete Carroll coaching tree (Carroll's tree has spread far and wide and Canales brings that branch to Charlotte).
known_for: Known for getting the best from quarterbacks (Geno Smith and Baker Mayfield had career seasons with him).

tree: Sean Payton, who hired him in 2023: quarterbacks coach, then pass game coordinator, promoted to offensive coordinator.
known_for: Runs Sean Payton's offense, which he says is mostly unchanged, and quarterback Bo Nix credits him with helping keep things simple.

tree: Kyle Shanahan and Robert Saleh.
known_for: Keeps defense simple, with predictable pre-snap looks, heavy zone coverage, little blitzing and a wide-9 front.

tree: Sean Payton (New Orleans and Denver) and Ben Johnson (Chicago).
known_for: Emphasizes explosive plays, with new shifts and motions and a heavy focus on snap cadence.
Leans on press-man coverage and simulated pressures, with defensive backs playing close to the action. One analyst calls it a disguise zone scheme.
Wants an attacking, aggressive defense, and ran a base 4-3 as the Saints head coach.

tree: Kellen Moore. Worked with him at the Cowboys (from 2018; QBs coach 2020-22), Chargers (2023) and Eagles.

known_for: Ran a strong ground game in Arizona: second in yards per rush attempt and ninth in rushing yards from 2023 to 2025.

tree: Andy Reid: spent 10 seasons with Reid in Kansas City, five as running backs coach (2013-17) and five as offensive coordinator (2018-22), and returned as OC in 2026.
known_for: His Chiefs offenses finished no lower than sixth in the NFL in scoring during his five seasons as coordinator, winning two Super Bowls.

tree: Kevin O'Connell (Vikings), in the Sean McVay coaching tree.

known_for: The Titans move from a 3-4 to his 4-3 defense, which relies on fast linebackers, ball-hawking defensive backs and pressure on the quarterback without blitzing much.
Known for how and when he blitzes, going after offenses when they are struggling.
His defense mixes 3-4 and 4-3 looks and varies fronts and coverages, because he says modern defenses need that variety.

tree: Mike Macdonald (together they helped craft the Ravens' defensive scheme) and the Harbaugh brothers, John and Jim.
known_for: Runs a 3-4 defense built on versatility and disguise, and does not blitz much (about one extra rusher every five snaps with the Chargers).
Plays physical football: his teams want to control the line of scrimmage and wear defenses down, with a commitment to running the football.

tree: Sean Payton tree (Brady says he comes from it).
Mike Zimmer (Minnesota) and Matt Eberflus before Philadelphia; his Eagles defense was a Fangio-adjacent system.
known_for: Does not tie himself to one scheme: keeps a few staples and only calls what his players can do. He ran a base 3-4 in Arizona and a 4-3 with some 3-4 elements in Philadelphia.

tree: Bill Belichick (worked for him 15 years, through all six Super Bowl wins)

known_for: Uses a lot of tempo, motions and shifts to stress defenses every week.

tree: Aaron Glenn, who mentored him and ran the Lions defense for four seasons before Sheppard took over.
known_for: Keeps the Lions' man-heavy coverage defense, a simple system he calls versatile and adaptable, and has used more zone recently.

tree: Sean McVay / Jon Gruden. His offense descends from Mike Shanahan's system.
known_for: Offense built on pre-snap motion, three-receiver sets, a zone run game and play action, in a quarterback-friendly system. Wants a run game that is "multiple", not only zone.
Wants a detailed, tough, physical team and says physicality is earned.

tree: Kyle Shanahan / Gary Kubiak.

known_for: Runs Dallas's run game, with full say over that part of the weekly plan, mixing outside zone and gap schemes by matchup.
Builds the offense around a strong running game that sets up deep passes off play action.

tree: Mike Shanahan / Gary Kubiak. Kubiak was Mike Shanahan's Broncos offensive coordinator and hired Kyle as Texans wide receivers coach in 2006.
known_for: Outside zone is the home-base run play, and play action is a main way the offense attacks defenses.

tree: Sean McVay (Coen and Kevin O'Connell worked under McVay with the Rams); Buccaneers offensive coordinator in 2024.

known_for: Changes fronts and coverages week to week based on the opponent, and plans to use more man coverage. He played man about a quarter of the time in Cincinnati.

tree: Jim Schwartz and Mike Zimmer: Burke worked for both.
known_for: Runs an attacking 4-3 defense with a penetrating defensive line (his one-word description of it was "attack").

tree: Mike and Kyle Shanahan, Gary Kubiak, and Sean McVay's coaching tree.
known_for: Runs the outside-zone run game paired with play-action passes off it, the same system the Shanahan, Kubiak and McVay offenses use.

tree: John Harbaugh (Ravens; Macdonald was his protege) / Wink Martindale (Macdonald coached under him 2018-21 and learned many blitzes from him). Early-down looks share similarities with Fangio's system.
known_for: Disguises coverage by showing two deep safeties and rotating after the snap. Gets pressure with four rushers and simulated pressures rather than lots of blitzes.
Passing game built around spacing, tempo, timing and quarterback control.

tree: Kyle Shanahan (five seasons on his 49ers staff)
known_for: Wide-zone running game that relies on linemen who move quickly and together.

tree: Jeff Ulbrich: coached under him with the Jets and learned his relationship-first approach to leading.
known_for: Says the identity is style over scheme, playing hard, fast, violent and smart, and builds from Jim Schwartz's defense around what players do well.

tree: Urban Meyer / Bill O'Brien (never on a Belichick staff)
known_for: Hands-on coach who builds a hard-working, hard-nosed culture, built on four pillars including "effort and finish".

tree: Matt Campbell / Sean McVay. Iowa State staff from 2018 (offensive coordinator from 2022); now on McVay's Rams staff.
Matt LaFleur: Packers offensive coordinator 2019-21 and defensive analyst in 2025.
Bill Belichick (Patriots), then Sean McVay with the Rams.
known_for: Not tied to one system: says the offense is Houston's own, built around the quarterback and roster, with roots in the Patriots and Rams.

tree: Jonathan Gannon: two seasons on the Eagles staff under Gannon, then followed him to Arizona.
known_for: Known for developing linebackers; his Arizona defense leans on Quarters coverage, and the Cardinals led the NFL in Quarters usage in 2023.

tree: Frank Reich (Colts offensive coordinator under him for three seasons)

known_for: Runs a 3-4 base defense in Pittsburgh, like the Tomlin and LeBeau Steelers defenses, and wants an intimidating style of play.

tree: Sean Payton: Saints offensive coordinator for most of 2006-2023, then senior offensive assistant with Payton in Denver.

known_for: Uses five-man fronts (a fifth player on the line to create pre-snap uncertainty), blitzes more often than Saleh did, disguises coverage and adds hybrid positions like the "star" nickel defender and the "fever backer".

tree: Steve Spagnuolo / Brian Flores / Mike Macdonald
known_for: Moves the Raiders from a 4-3 to a 3-4 base, though Kubiak says they can also play four down linemen.

tree: Kyle Shanahan (49ers defensive coordinator 2017-20 and again in 2025)
Jeff Hafley. Worked with him at Ohio State, Boston College (linebackers coach and defensive coordinator) and Green Bay (defensive assistant, linebackers coach).
known_for: Wants Miami's defense to be multiple and to fit the strengths of its players.

tree: Matt LaFleur (Packers quarterbacks coach from 2024) / Sean McVay (Rams, 2017). His scheme has roots in the McVay system.
known_for: Installing a version of the Shanahan/McVay offense, blended with what the Eagles have run under Sirianni.
Uses a lot of pre-snap motion and play action, pairing run and pass concepts. Has added 13-personnel sets and moved to more under-center gap runs.

tree: Bill Parcells (Payton is described as a Parcells protege).
known_for: Likes to run the ball to set up the pass.
Builds the offense around his quarterback's strengths ("throw to score points and run to win") and is credited with a strong ground attack.

tree: Jim Johnson: started under Johnson as a position coach on the Eagles defense in the late 1990s.
known_for: Brings heavy, creative pressure (including blitzes the team has not practiced lately) with cornerbacks on one-on-one islands, a style learned from Johnson. He has four Super Bowl rings as a coordinator.

tree: Bruce Arians (head coach in Tampa Bay while Bowles ran the defense)
known_for: Runs an attacking, one-gap defense and is described as blitz-heavy.
Fits his scheme to his players' talents. His Baltimore offense was among the league's most explosive and had the highest designed run rate in the NFL.

tree: Pete Carroll: on Carroll's Seattle staff in 2012 with Gus Bradley, Marquand Manuel and Robert Saleh.
known_for: Says his defense is defined more by how versatile its players are than by scheme.
Runs an aggressive attack-style defense with a lot of pressure and man coverage, and goes to zone when the matchup calls for it.

tree: Vic Fangio (root of his own tree; Brandon Staley, Joe Barry and Sean Desai are in it)
known_for: Plays two-high safety shells to take away deep throws and invite runs into lighter boxes, and disguises coverage, rotating between quarters and other coverages.

tree: Kevin O'Connell. Rams tight ends coach 2019-20 and pass game coordinator for O'Connell in 2021; joined Minnesota as OC in 2022.
Sean McVay (his stated background)
known_for: Builds the offense around his players ("players over plays"), adapting to the quarterback, line and skill group. Uses pre-snap motion with purpose and pairs the run and pass games.

tree: Sean McVay: assistant wide receivers coach on McVay's 2017 Rams staff, then quarterbacks coach in 2018.
known_for: Runs a more spread-out version of McVay's offense, built around Joe Burrow, with fewer bunch sets and much less pre-snap motion than McVay.

tree: Mike Vrabel (Titans staff 2020-23, then Patriots linebackers coach and defensive coordinator)
known_for: Aggressive, blitz-heavy defense: the Patriots blitzed in the postseason and showed pressure before the snap, then dropped rushers into coverage. Built around man coverage with well-timed zone blitzes and reflects Vrabel's aggressive "effort and finish" identity.
